newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African cabinet seen split over waste watchdog.
newsitem.headline: S.African cabinet seen split over waste watchdog.

text.p: South African government departments are split over which of them should control pollution from such sources as gold mines, politicians were told on Wednesday.

Tinus Joubert, deputy director in charge of waste at the department of the environment, told a parliamentary committee that he questioned whether the department of mineral affairs and energy should retain its authority over pollution generated by mining.
"That department is specifically responsible for promoting the exploitation of minerals... but that same department is responsible to look after the environmental aspects of mining," Joubert said.
"Can one department be player and referee at the same time? This is a contentious issue, and it's being debated between the ministers concerned," he said.

"There's a lot of loopholes that make it possible for the mining industry to go ahead and mine, with the approval of minerals and energy, without having a clear picture of what it will do to the environment."

Joubert said a white paper on pollution and waste management due to go before parliament at the end of August would seek to make the department of the environment the "lead agent" in dealing with these issues.
He added that landfills were the responsibility of the department of water affairs and forestry.
The chairwoman of the committee, Gwen Mahlangu, said the lead agent proposal had created "a lot of tension" between ministries but she did not elaborate.
